ft01-rusningen.title: The rush
ft01-rusningen.body: It is nearly seven, and the queue grows along the awning. The grill is full, and the first guest looks at the sausage in their hand.

steps.question: Why does a sausage split when it is grilled too hot?

a.label: Because it is too old.
a.explanation: Age does not split a sausage. The steam inside does.

b.label: Because the water inside boils and the pressure bursts the casing before the middle is hot.
b.explanation: Right. The water turns to steam, the pressure bursts the casing, and the juice runs out while the middle is still cold.

c.label: Because the salt melts.
c.explanation: Salt does not melt at grill heat. It is the water that boils.

d.label: Because the grill is too dirty, so old burnt fat sticks to the casing and tears it open as the sausage is turned.
d.explanation: A dirty grill gives a burnt taste but does not split the sausage.

fail.outcome: A sausage splits on the grill, and the next in the queue has to wait.

steps.question: The queue is long, and a guest says the sausage is cold inside. What do you do?

a.label: Apologise, give a discount on the next purchase and promise that the rest of the evening’s sausages will be better.
a.explanation: The discount does not fix a cold sausage, and the next one may be the same.

b.label: Swap it at once for one that is hot through, and check the grill’s heat and pace.
b.explanation: Right. The guest gets a hot sausage, and you fix the cause instead of hoping the queue can wait.

c.label: Say it is meant to be like that.
c.explanation: A sausage should be hot through. The guest leaves, and the reputation goes with them.

d.label: Grill it another minute and hand back the same one.
d.explanation: A minute rarely heats the middle, and the queue grows meanwhile.

fail.outcome: The guest leaves with the cold sausage, and others in the queue see it.

steps.question: How do you grill the sausages before the evening rush?

a.label: On the highest heat, so it goes quickly and the queue moves.
a.explanation: High heat splits the sausages before they are hot inside, and the queue waits for new ones.

fail.outcome: The sausages split in the rush, and the queue grows impatient.

b.label: Medium heat, turning often, so they don't split.
b.explanation: Right. Medium heat and frequent turning give sausages that are hot through and stay whole.

c.label: In cold water first, then on high heat to finish them.
c.explanation: The water takes time, and the high heat splits them anyway.

d.label: On one side only, so they keep their juices.
d.explanation: Then the sausage is burnt on one side and cold on the other.

fail.outcome: The sausages split in the rush, and the queue grows impatient.
The sausages split in the rush, and the queue grows impatient.

success.outcome: The sausages are hot through and whole, and the queue moves.

staff.outcome: The helper lowers the heat and swaps the sausage, but the queue had time to grow.

ft02-drycken.title: The drink with it
ft02-drycken.body: A guest at the hatch wants something to drink with the sausage and asks what you recommend.

steps.question: Why does a bitter, sparkling drink suit a salty, fatty sausage?

a.label: The bitterness makes the sausage sweeter.
a.explanation: Bitterness does not make food sweeter. It is the interplay of salt, bitterness and fat that works.

b.label: The salt softens the bitterness, and the bitterness and bubbles cut through the fat.
b.explanation: Right. The salt in the sausage softens the bitterness, and bitterness and bubbles clear the fat between bites.

c.label: The bubbles warm the sausage.
c.explanation: The bubbles do not change the sausage’s temperature. They clear the fat from the mouth.

d.label: They do not go together; sausage should be eaten with water, as the bubbles and bitterness drown out the spices.
d.explanation: Water is fine, but a bitter, sparkling drink lifts the sausage through the salt and the fat.

fail.outcome: The guest takes a sweet soda and leaves half the sausage.

steps.question: It starts to rain, and the queue gets short. What do you do?

a.label: Close for the evening.
a.explanation: Rain often passes, and those who come go to another truck.

b.label: Slow the grill to the queue’s pace, put out the awning and offer something hot to drink.
b.explanation: Right. You waste no sausages, the guests stay dry, and the evening can pick up again.

c.label: Grill as usual; people will come.
c.explanation: The sausages sit there and are thrown away at the end of the evening.

d.label: Cut the price in half.
d.explanation: Half price draws few in the rain and costs you on every other sale.

fail.outcome: The sausages sit in the rain and are thrown away.

steps.question: Which drink do you suggest with a spicy grilled sausage to a guest who does not drink alcohol?

a.label: Water, because nothing else goes with spicy food.
a.explanation: Water works, but there are alcohol-free drinks that suit the sausage better.

b.label: Alcohol-free beer or something sparkling and bitter, like tonic.
b.explanation: Right. The bitterness and bubbles do what they do in a beer: they meet the salt and cut through the fat.

c.label: A sweet fruit soda to cool down after the hot sausage.
c.explanation: The sweetness clashes with the spices and makes the sausage feel heavier.

fail.outcome: The guest gets a drink that does not suit and buys no more.

d.label: A glass of cold milk to calm the heat of the spices.
d.explanation: Milk calms the heat but does nothing for the salt and the fat.

fail.outcome: The guest gets a drink that does not suit and buys no more.
The guest gets a drink that does not suit and buys no more.

success.outcome: The guest takes a drink with the sausage and comes back for another.

staff.outcome: The helper suggests a drink, and the evening moves on.

ft03-rullen.title: The roll
ft03-rullen.body: A group orders flatbread rolls, and one of them has had too much to drink.

steps.question: What holds a grilled sausage together, so that it does not fall apart on the grill?

a.label: The flour in the mixture, which swells in the heat and holds the fat and water together.
a.explanation: Flour binds a little water, but it is not what holds the sausage together.

b.label: The salt, which draws out the meat proteins so they bind fat and water.
b.explanation: Right. Salt draws out the proteins in the meat, and they hold fat and water together as the sausage heats.

c.label: The smoke.
c.explanation: Smoke gives flavour and colour, but binds nothing.

d.label: The casing.
d.explanation: The casing holds the shape on the outside; the inside is held together by the proteins the salt draws out.

fail.outcome: The roll falls apart in the guest’s hand.

steps.question: A drunk guest becomes rude to your helper at the hatch. What do you do?

a.label: Let the helper deal with it.
a.explanation: The helper is left alone with it, and you are the one responsible for the hatch.

b.label: Step in yourself, calmly, refuse further service if needed, and support the helper afterwards.
b.explanation: Right. You protect the helper, set a calm limit and make sure it does not stay with the one who took the brunt.

c.label: Give the guest a free sausage so he leaves.
c.explanation: It teaches the guest that rudeness pays, and the helper gets no help.

d.label: Call the police straight away.
d.explanation: The police are needed if it turns to threats or violence. First you set a calm limit yourself.

fail.outcome: The guest carries on, and the helper is left alone with it.

steps.question: How do you make a flatbread roll that holds together when the guest eats it standing?

a.label: Plenty of prawn salad on top, so it's juicy all the way.
a.explanation: Prawn salad on top makes the roll soggy, and it falls apart.

fail.outcome: The roll spills, and the guest wants a new one.

b.label: Mash as a bed, then sausage, prawn salad, onion; rolled tight.
b.explanation: Right. The mash holds the sausage, and a tight roll with the edge underneath holds in the hand.

c.label: Roll it loosely, so the guest can open it and see inside.
c.explanation: A loose roll opens by itself while the guest eats.

fail.outcome: The roll spills, and the guest wants a new one.

d.label: Cut it in two, so it's easier to hold.
d.explanation: Cut in two, the filling runs out of both ends.

fail.outcome: The roll spills, and the guest wants a new one.

success.outcome: The rolls hold, and the group moves on calmly.

staff.outcome: The helper deals with the group, but is shaken.

ft04-leveransen.title: The delivery
ft04-leveransen.body: The supplier has brought tonight’s sausages and offers a cheaper batch for next week.

steps.question: What is the casing of a grilled sausage usually made of?

a.label: Plastic.
a.explanation: Plastic casings exist, but on a sausage eaten with its skin it is gut or collagen.

b.label: Natural casing from pig or sheep, or an edible collagen casing.
b.explanation: Right. A grilling sausage has natural casing or an edible collagen casing.

c.label: Paper, a thin baking paper the sausage is shaped in and that is pulled off before grilling.
c.explanation: Paper does not hold on the grill.

d.label: Starch.
d.explanation: Starch may be in the mixture, not in the casing.

fail.outcome: You accept the sausages without knowing what they are made of.

steps.question: A supplier offers cheaper sausage with no information on where the meat comes from. What do you weigh?

a.label: Only the price; the guests will not notice.
a.explanation: Guests ask, and then you have no answer.

b.label: The price against what you can tell the guest about origin and against your reputation, and you ask the supplier about origin and meat content.
b.explanation: Right. You do the sums, but you ask first, so that you can stand behind what you sell.

c.label: Switch at once, without asking.
c.explanation: You do not know what you sell, and it shows when a guest asks.

d.label: Keep the old one without doing the sums.
d.explanation: It may be right, but you do not know why.

fail.outcome: You have no answer when a guest asks about the sausage.

steps.question: How many sausages do you have out before the seven o’clock rush?

a.label: All you have, so nothing is missing when the big queue comes.
a.explanation: What does not sell in time stands too long.

fail.outcome: The sausages sit too long before the rush.

b.label: Enough for the next half hour's queue, topped up evenly.
b.explanation: Right. The right amount out and even topping up give hot sausages without waste.

c.label: One at a time, so every sausage is freshly grilled.
c.explanation: The queue waits for every sausage.

d.label: None; everything is grilled once the guest has ordered.
d.explanation: The waits get long when the queue arrives.

fail.outcome: The sausages sit too long before the rush.
The sausages sit too long before the rush.

success.outcome: You know what you sell, and there is just enough ready when the queue comes.

staff.outcome: The helper takes the delivery, but no one asks where it comes from.

ft07-ursprunget.title: Where it comes from
ft07-ursprunget.body: A guest reads the packet behind the hatch and starts asking about the sausage while you take payment.

steps.question: What does the meat content on a sausage packet mean?

a.label: How much of the sausage is pork, counted by weight before it is grilled.
a.explanation: The meat content does not say which animal the meat is from.

b.label: What share of the sausage is meat, according to the recipe.
b.explanation: Right. The meat content is the share of meat in the recipe.

c.label: How much fat the sausage contains.
c.explanation: The fat content is listed separately. The meat content is the share of meat.

d.label: Where the meat comes from.
d.explanation: The origin is listed separately. The meat content is the share of meat.

fail.outcome: You cannot say what is in the sausage.

steps.question: A guest asks if the sausage is Swedish. The packet says "Made in Sweden". What do you answer?

a.label: Yes, it is Swedish.
a.explanation: "Made in Sweden" says where the sausage was made, not where the meat comes from.

b.label: That it is made in Sweden, but that this does not say where the meat comes from, and that you can find out.
b.explanation: Right. It is the difference between where something is made and where the ingredient comes from.

c.label: No, so it is foreign.
c.explanation: You do not know that. The meat may well be Swedish.

d.label: That it does not matter.
d.explanation: It matters to the guest who asks.

fail.outcome: The guest leaves without knowing what she bought.

steps.question: You take payment and serve sausages at the same hatch. How do you work?

a.label: Wipe your hands on the apron between each payment and sausage.
a.explanation: The apron does not remove what comes with the money.

fail.outcome: Money and food get mixed at the hatch.

b.label: Use tongs for the food, never the hand that takes money, or change gloves.
b.explanation: Right. Money and food are kept apart, with the tongs or fresh gloves.

c.label: Take payment first and serve afterwards, with the same gloves.
c.explanation: The gloves carry what they have touched.

d.label: Let the customer take the sausage themselves, with a napkin.
d.explanation: Then more hands touch the food.

fail.outcome: Money and food get mixed at the hatch.
Money and food get mixed at the hatch.

success.outcome: The guest gets an honest answer and buys another sausage.

staff.outcome: The helper answers as best they can.

ft05-allergin.title: The allergy
ft05-allergin.body: A guest at the hatch says she has an allergy, and at the same time the cool box shows too high a temperature.

steps.question: Which of the extras at the hatch contain one of the fourteen allergens that must be declared?

a.label: Only the bread.
a.explanation: The bread has gluten, but there are more.

b.label: Only the prawn salad.
b.explanation: The prawn salad has crustaceans and egg, but there are more.

c.label: The mustard, the bread (gluten), the prawn salad (crustaceans and egg) and the mash (milk).
c.explanation: Right. And the sausage itself can contain allergens, such as milk, mustard or celery, so read the packaging.

d.label: None; sausage stands are exempt because the food is sold unpackaged over the counter straight to the guest.
d.explanation: No one is exempt. Anyone selling food must be able to answer.

fail.outcome: The guest gets the wrong answer about the extras.

steps.question: A guest asks if the sausage contains nuts. You are not sure. What do you do?

a.label: Say no; it usually does not.
a.explanation: A guess can be dangerous for someone with an allergy.

b.label: Say you do not know for sure, show the ingredient list on the packaging or advise against it.
b.explanation: Right. Honesty and the packaging, and better a no than a guess.

c.label: Say yes to be safe.
c.explanation: It is not true, and the guest gets no help choosing.

d.label: Ask another guest.
d.explanation: The other guest does not know either.

fail.outcome: The guest gets a guess instead of an answer.

steps.question: The cool box shows +11 °C in the middle of the evening. What do you do first?

a.label: Carry on as usual; it's only one evening and the box still cools a little.
a.explanation: Food kept too warm can become unsafe to eat, even in one evening.

fail.outcome: The goods stay too warm for the rest of the evening.

b.label: Move the goods to at most +8 °C, log it and judge the rest.
b.explanation: Right. Get it cold first, then make the note and judge what has stood warm.

c.label: Close the hatch for the evening and throw out everything in the box.
c.explanation: That does not save the goods. The cold has to come first.

fail.outcome: The goods stay too warm for the rest of the evening.

d.label: Put ice on top of the lid and hope the temperature drops again.
d.explanation: Ice on the lid hardly cools what is inside the box.

fail.outcome: The goods stay too warm for the rest of the evening.
The goods stay too warm for the rest of the evening.

success.outcome: The guest knows what she can eat, and the cooling holds.

staff.outcome: The helper reads the packaging and moves the goods, but the guest has to wait.

ft06-stangningen.title: Closing time
ft06-stangningen.body: The queue has gone, there are sausages left in the warmer, and a last guest reads the packet.

steps.question: What is required for a sausage to be labelled "Meat from Sweden"?

a.label: That the sausage is made in Sweden, even if the meat in it may come from another country.
a.explanation: Where it is made says nothing about where the animals come from.

b.label: That the meat comes from animals born, reared and slaughtered in Sweden.
b.explanation: Right. The label is about the animals, not the factory.

c.label: That the sausage is sold in Sweden.
c.explanation: Where it is sold does not matter to the label.

d.label: That the spices are Swedish.
d.explanation: The label is about the meat.

fail.outcome: The guest gets the wrong answer about the label.

steps.question: The evening is over, and there are ten grilled sausages left. What do you do?

a.label: Chills them in the cool box and sells them tomorrow.
a.explanation: Hot-held food that is left over should be thrown away. It has already been held hot for hours, and cooling and reheating it adds to the risk.

b.label: Throw away those that stood in the warmer, and plan fewer for the next evening by how the queue went.
b.explanation: Right. What has stood hot is thrown away, and next evening you grill to the queue.

c.label: Give them to the helper to take home, without thinking about how long or at what heat they have been kept.
c.explanation: Eating it at home does not make the food safer.

d.label: Put them back in the packet.
d.explanation: The sausages have been held hot for hours. Putting them back in the packet does not make them safe again.

fail.outcome: What was left over is handled wrongly.

steps.question: The sausages have been in the warmer since opening. What do you do?

a.label: Sell them while they look fine and no guest has complained of the taste.
a.explanation: How they look does not tell you whether they have been kept hot enough.

fail.outcome: Sausage that has stood too long is sold on.

b.label: Check: at least +60 °C, no more than a few hours, else bin them.
b.explanation: Right. Temperature and time decide, not looks.

c.label: Grill them once more, so they're hot again before they are sold.
c.explanation: That does not rescue what has stood too cool for too long.

fail.outcome: Sausage that has stood too long is sold on.

d.label: Put them in the fridge and sell them tomorrow as the first of the day.
d.explanation: Food that has been kept hot should not be chilled and sold again.

fail.outcome: Sausage that has stood too long is sold on.
Sausage that has stood too long is sold on.

success.outcome: What stood hot is thrown away, and the next evening is planned by the queue.

staff.outcome: The helper throws the leftovers away, but no one plans the next evening.
